findings.claim: This repo's docs-layout rule keeps the old sentence next to the new one: 'Its index page, README.md at the top of docs/, lists every page. Its index page, README.md at the top of docs/, links each folder's own README.md index'. The first sentence is now false and contradicts the second. The shipped claude and antigravity copies got it right.

Row r7's fails_when includes 'a page with no front matter fails', but neither field_shape test has a page without front matter: test_field_shape_good_and_absent_pass overwrites upgrade.md with full front matter, and install.md has a description. The name says 'absent' but no absent case is checked. Other tests (check_fix) cover it indirectly, but not the row's command.

The tutorial still says every command was run with kmctl 0.1.0 and the output is what it printed, but the new check / check --fix output (warning level, 'fixed', '1 failed, 1 warning') only exists from this change on.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan says.

Generated folder indexes with a marker, `kmctl check --fix`, the error for a missing or stale folder index, the warning level for a root index with no folder link, hand-written indexes left alone with a warning, optional OKF fields on docs pages with shape checks, docs pages in `review due` (also without `.okf/`), the `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` hook and the migrated docs/ all work.
I re-ran the gates and they are green.

Three findings, none blocking: a leftover false sentence in this repo's docs-layout rule, an r7 test whose "absent front matter" case has no absent front matter, and a tutorial version claim the new output makes false.
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree gave "stamp green: d541da4729b6c4e7c085b95168d74ebf029ec6668d5f31ff5d849625bd985578".
lint, format, tests and integration passed, and so did every row r1-r9, r11-r13.
Code read in full: `src/kmctl/docs_index.py`, plus the diffs to `checks.py`, `docs.py`, `scaffold.py`, `review_due.py`, `kinds.py`, `briefing.py` and `__init__.py`.
I checked the paths that could go wrong.
`missing_ok` stops a second error when the root links a missing folder index.
`is_generated` handles non-UTF-8 and empty files.
A hand-written index is never written by `fix_folder_indexes`, `new_doc` or `scaffold`.
`--fix` prints its "fixed" lines to stderr under `--json`.
A docs page's baseline is its latest `verified` date or, with none, its last commit.
`_resolve` is called with okf=root, so a leading `/` means the repo root.

Ran it by hand in a scratch repo: init, add an unindexed how-to, `check` (1 error, 1 warning, exit 1), `check --fix` (writes the index, passes with 1 warning), add the root link (clean), then `new doc` with a description holding `:` and `[ ]`.
The YAML is quoted, the index entry is right and the root link was added.
The output matches the tutorial text.
Rows.
r1: the snapshot diff proves nothing else changes, and the second run is idempotent.
r2: one error for each folder case, the fix names `--fix`, and the out-of-folder pages are errors.
r3: check and action test (exit 0, the warning shows in the summary).
r4: all three writers leave the file unchanged, and check warns with exit 0.
r5: fields, no `verified`, the folder index, update creates indexes and leaves the root index alone.
r6: stale, source changed after the page's commit and after `verified`, no `.okf/`, the docs/ id prefix and the `--json` keys.
r7: see f2.
r8, r9, r11 (offline shape plus a real prek run from a scratch repo pinned to a commit of a copy), r12, r13: each asserts its fails_when.
r10 (judgment): ADR 0022 says in plain words why docs/ is not a bundle.
Diataxis sorts by what the reader wants to do, OKF by kind of knowledge, users would see YAML they never asked for, and the split is by reader.
Folder indexes are generated because "a script can write it, so a script does".
The root stays hand-written because it "is where a person explains the docs".
The reasoning matches the plan.
The rules, the commands reference and the tutorial agree with it.
Pass.

Consistency: the manifesto I4 and its kmctl description, the architecture overview, the commands reference, the shipped rules, the CLAUDE.md block, the briefing, the write-docs, audit and auditor prompts and the kinds schema all agree with the code, except f1 and f3.
f1: `.claude/rules/docs-layout.md` lines 10-13 kept "lists every page" and added the new sentence after it, so the rule contradicts itself.
Delete the old sentence, as the two shipped copies already do.
f2: r7's command never checks a page with no front matter.
Give `test_field_shape_good_and_absent_pass` one page with no front matter (for example, leave `_docs`' upgrade.md alone and write the good front matter to a third page).
f3: the tutorial's "run ... with kmctl 0.1.0" claim no longer holds for the new check / check --fix output.
Say which version printed it.
README.md and the how-to pin `rev: v0.3.0` for the new hook.
That tag does not have `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`.
It follows the repo's habit of bumping every pin at release, so I did not raise it as a finding.
Check it at release time.
